**ID:** Snp 5.11 (PTS Snp 211)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)

**Title (Pali):** Kappamāṇavapucchā

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kappamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Kappa") is a verse discourse located in the *Pārāyaṇavagga*, the fifth chapter of the *Suttanipāta* (Snp 5.11, PTS Snp 211), beginning around verse 1092 [Hazra 1994; Norman 1997–2001]. In this sutta, the student Kappa addresses the Buddha to ask about the island that provides refuge amidst the overwhelming flood and the perils of birth. Secondary treatments frequently list the work as one of the successive question-dialogues (*pucchā*) of the *Pārāyaṇavagga* [Hazra 1994; Saddhatissa 2013].
